correctness.rationale: For any nonempty finite poset P, odd q, each commuting k-tuple of involutions in its incidence algebra yields orthogonal sign-character idempotents e_eps=2^(-k)Π_i(1+eps_i a_i), which are conjugate to diagonal sign projectors by explicit unit u=Σ_eps e_eps d_eps∈1+J. The diagonal coloring c:P->[2^k] is invariant under unipotent conjugation; stabilizer size q^(m-d(c)) for d(c) differently colored comparable pairs, so C_k=Σ_c q^d(c)=Σ_(F⊆E)q^(m-|F|)(1-q)^|F|(2^k)^κ(F), the exact Potts/random-cluster expansion. Every commuting clique embeds into a full diagonal sign subgroup (size 2^n), whose unipotent normalizer is trivial, giving exactly q^m maximal cliques. Stirling inversion counts distinct commuting subsets; all odd q and k recover Tutte, and q→∞ normalized C_k approaches chromatic polynomial at 2^k. Independent direct F3 three-element-chain enumeration found 56 involutions and 976 ordered commuting pairs, matching Potts formula. General proof rests on idempotent conjugation, not finite enumeration.
